profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap record, tagged Aligned Energy Data Center, sits at coordinates that correspond closely to 2500 West Union Hills Drive in Phoenix, Arizona, the 55-acre flagship address Aligned Data Centers own Phoenix location page lists for its cluster of buildings on that campus, referenced in company materials as the PHX-01, PHX-02, PHX-03, and PHX-05 group. Aligned own site discloses campus-level infrastructure standards for the Phoenix market, including a Tier III design approach with 3 megawatt generators and 2 megawatt uninterruptible power supply units per building, but does not break out individual capacity or square footage figures per building on that page, and no dedicated press release matching this exact coordinate to one specific building code among PHX-01 through PHX-05 could be located this session. A separate Aligned facility in the Phoenix market, PHX-06, sits at a distinct Chandler, Arizona address and earned Three Green Globes sustainability certification per a July 2025 Aligned press release, but that is a different building from this Union Hills campus record and should not be conflated with it. Given this ambiguity, no specific capacity, square footage, or building-code assignment beyond the general Union Hills campus location is claimed here. Aligned, formerly known as Aligned Energy, the name still reflected in this record OpenStreetMap tag, describes its overall footprint today as more than fifty campuses and roughly five gigawatts of contracted and available capacity across the Americas, with Latin American operations run under the ODATA brand. Ownership has shifted substantially over the company history, most recently with an October 2025 agreement for a consortium called AI Infrastructure Partnership, combining BlackRock Global Infrastructure Partners and MGX, to acquire all of Aligned equity from majority owner Macquarie Asset Management and its co-investors in a deal valued near 40 billion dollars, with a close indicated around July 2026 in Aligned own materials though not independently confirmed by a dedicated press release this session.

reading.body:
This facility publishes 200,000 square feet of technical space but no power capacity figure, making it impossible to assess its relevance to AI infrastructure or compare it to other Arizona data centers.

The operator's press release describes a Phase II expansion with a planned 1.15 power usage effectiveness ratio and rack densities up to 50 kilowatts per unit. These specifications indicate high-density design appropriate for compute workloads. Without a published megawatt figure, however, this site cannot place the facility in Arizona's mapped inventory or determine whether it serves AI tenants versus other workloads.

Arizona has 56 tracked facilities, but only four publish power capacity. This facility joins a larger pattern where operator disclosure varies widely. Size in square footage does not predict power draw or compute density, because cooling approach, voltage delivery, and rack configuration differ across data centers. A reader evaluating this campus would require the operator to publish IT load in megawatts before making siting or investment decisions.

The parent company, Aligned Data Centers, operates 87 facilities across 51 campuses with stated 6.4 gigawatts of capacity and is undergoing a $40 billion ownership transfer. The Phoenix expansion alone claims up to 60 megawatts at full buildout. Publication of this site-level capacity would clarify whether Aligned's portfolio growth is concentrated in a few large campuses or distributed across many smaller ones, which matters for understanding whether grid constraints bind differently by region.
